title: Nonconstant maps of smooth proper curves and function-field embeddings
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field], [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $X,Y$ be smooth proper integral $k$-curves of dimension one [def-sc-curves], [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Their function fields $k(X),k(Y)$ [def-sc-function-field] are finitely generated extensions of $k$ of transcendence degree one [def-pc-field-extension], [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. A $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$ is called nonconstant when it does not factor through a $k$-rational point of $Y$. Every such $f$ sends the generic point of $X$ to that of $Y$ and induces a $k$-embedding $f^*:k(Y)\hookrightarrow k(X)$; the resulting extension $k(X)/f^*k(Y)$ is finite [def-pc-field-tower]. The assignment $f\mapsto f^*$ is a bijection between nonconstant $k$-morphisms $X\to Y$ and $k$-embeddings $k(Y)\hookrightarrow k(X)$. It respects identities and composition: $(g\circ f)^*=f^*\circ g^*$ whenever $g:Y\to Z$ is another nonconstant morphism between such curves.

source.place: Tag 0BY1 (curves-theorem-curves-rational-maps), equivalence of categories (1) and (6) and the fully faithful functor in the third paragraph of its proof; smooth curves are nonsingular. Finiteness follows from finite generation and transcendence degree one.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-curve-function-field-arithmetic] to $X$ and $Y$ (integral, finite type, dimension one). This gives finite generation and transcendence degree one for both function fields.

source.place: Tag 0BY1 (curves-theorem-curves-rational-maps), third proof paragraph; explicit generic-point construction, valuative extension and equalizer uniqueness

proof.text: For a nonconstant $f:X\to Y$, [lem-sfb-curve-nonconstant-generic-criterion] gives $f(\eta_X)=\eta_Y$ and its actual generic-stalk $k$-embedding $f^*$. Apply the field-extension clause of [lem-sfb-curve-function-field-arithmetic] to this embedding: $[k(X):f^*k(Y)]<\infty$.

source.place: Tag 0BY1 (curves-theorem-curves-rational-maps), third proof paragraph; explicit generic-point construction, valuative extension and equalizer uniqueness

proof.text: Given a $k$-embedding $\varphi:k(Y)\hookrightarrow k(X)$, $X$ is connected because it is irreducible. Thus [lem-sfb-smooth-curve-embedding-extension] gives $F:X\to Y$ with $F(\eta_X)=\eta_Y$ and $F^*=\varphi$. By [lem-sfb-curve-nonconstant-generic-criterion], $F$ is nonconstant.

source.place: Tag 0BY1 (curves-theorem-curves-rational-maps), third proof paragraph; explicit generic-point construction, valuative extension and equalizer uniqueness

proof.text: If $f^*=g^*$, their generic restrictions coincide: on an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $\eta_Y$, both are given by $A\hookrightarrow k(Y)\xrightarrow{f^*}k(X)$, by [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. The map $i_X:\operatorname{Spec}k(X)\to X$ has dense image $\{\eta_X\}$ by [def-sc-generic-point]. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-separated-dominant-ext] with $T=X$, $W=\operatorname{Spec}k(X)$ and $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$: $X$ is reduced and $Y/k$ is separated since proper. Hence $f=g$; together with step 3 this proves bijectivity.

source.place: Tag 0BY1 (curves-theorem-curves-rational-maps), third proof paragraph; explicit generic-point construction, valuative extension and equalizer uniqueness

proof.text: The identity sends generic point to generic point; so do composites of two nonconstant maps, by [lem-sfb-curve-nonconstant-generic-criterion]. The same criterion shows these maps are nonconstant. On a germ represented by a section $a$, identity pullback fixes $a$, and composite pullback is successive pullback, by [def-pc-scheme] and [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Taking germs gives $(\operatorname{id}_X)^*=\operatorname{id}_{k(X)}$ and $(g\circ f)^*(a)=f^*(g^*(a))$.

lean.statement: theorem proper_curve_function_field_morphisms (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (X Y : Scheme.{u}) (sX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (sY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsIntegral X] [IsIntegral Y] [IsCurve sX] [IsCurve sY] [Smooth sX] [Smooth sY] [IsProper sX] [IsProper sY] (hXdim : topologicalKrullDim X = 1) (hYdim : topologicalKrullDim Y = 1) : (@IntermediateField.FG k _ X.functionField _ sX.curveFunctionFieldBaseMap.toAlgebra ⊤ ∧ @Algebra.trdeg k X.functionField _ _ sX.curveFunctionFieldBaseMap.toAlgebra = 1) ∧ (@IntermediateField.FG k _ Y.functionField _ sY.curveFunctionFieldBaseMap.toAlgebra ⊤ ∧ @Algebra.trdeg k Y.functionField _ _ sY.curveFunctionFieldBaseMap.toAlgebra = 1) ∧ (∀ (f : X ⟶ Y) (_ : f ≫ sY = sX) (_ : ¬ ∃ y : Spec (.of k) ⟶ Y, y ≫ sY = 𝟙 _ ∧ sX ≫ y = f), ∃ hf : f (genericPoint X) = genericPoint Y, Function.Injective (f.functionFieldMap hf).hom ∧ (f.functionFieldMap hf).hom.comp sY.curveFunctionFieldBaseMap = sX.curveFunctionFieldBaseMap ∧ @Module.Finite Y.functionField X.functionField _ _ (@Algebra.toModule _ _ _ _ (f.functionFieldMap hf).hom.toAlgebra)) ∧ (∀ φ : Y.functionField →+* X.functionField, φ.comp sY.curveFunctionFieldBaseMap = sX.curveFunctionFieldBaseMap → ∃! f : {f : X ⟶ Y // f ≫ sY = sX ∧ ¬ ∃ y : Spec (.of k) ⟶ Y, y ≫ sY = 𝟙 _ ∧ sX ≫ y = f}, ∃ hf : f.val (genericPoint X) = genericPoint Y, (f.val.functionFieldMap hf).hom = φ)
lean.note: The main theorem states the canonical generic-stalk correspondence by its graph (a unique nonconstant base morphism for every base-compatible field homomorphism), including finite generation, transcendence degree one and finiteness. Identity and composition are the other two theorem declarations. The sole helper constructs the scalar map k to the generic stalk from ΓSpecIso, the structure map on global sections, and the germ; no data is postponed.
